Bloomberg reported yesterday that Apple is collaborating with LG to develop new smart home accessories, which will be sold under the LG brand. Leaked images showcase the designs of a smart door lock, a thermostat, and a temperature sensor.

The images reveal three Home accessories Apple reportedly developed for LG

Next week, Apple is rumoured to announce a long-awaited major update to its Home product line. The company will unveil an all-new Apple TV 4K and HomePod mini, as well as a brand-new product category we've been calling the "HomePad."

However, Bloomberg's report yesterday sheds light on another piece of Apple's Home strategy. The company has partnered with LG to develop new Home accessories, which will be sold under the LG brand.

According to the report, these accessories include a smart door lock, thermostat, temperature sensor, video doorbell, indoor camera, outdoor camera, and a floodlight camera.

Today, leaker pdfu shared the first images of three of these products: a smart door lock, a smart thermostat, and a temperature sensor.

LateStage trending posts

LG, isn't that the TV brand that was caught monitoring users even after being powered off? Whatever happened to Apple's commitment to privacy?

pdfu also posted a thread on X revealing more details about these products.

For instance, the smart deadbolt features a rotary dial with features like "an LED ring around the touchpad, an audible chime when the door is left ajar, and lock volume adjustments," along with other capabilities such as automatic unlocking.

Mark Gurman notes that these new products may not be ready in time to launch alongside Apple's new HomePod and Apple TV. However, there's still a good chance Apple will mention these products at next week's event.

What are your thoughts on these smart home accessories designed by Apple and sold under the LG brand? Share your opinions in the comments section below.
